subject: VanguardCare - managed burst credit carveout (VP/CFO signoff required)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VanguardCare request — managed-burst credit + packaging clarification

Team —

Quick summary: VanguardCare (Sarah Li / Raj Patel) wants a one-off managed-burst credit and an accelerated onboarding concession tied to an expected multi-year commitment. They are proposing a 3-year deal with an initial pilot year that will have unpredictable burst traffic (up to 4x baseline) for clinical data ingest and inference. They asked explicitly for: a $150k managed-burst credit (to absorb token/spike cost during pilot) plus a 30% off list unit price for year 1, with a 3-year committed minimum.

Attachments: vanguardcare-term-sheet-v3.pdf (term details + pricing table), usage-forecast-q3.csv (customer-provided traffic profile).

Risks/points for exec review:
- Precedent: awarding a large, unconditional burst credit sets a pricing precedent for other pilot customers.
- Revenue recognition / accounting: large credits upstream will require schedule and possibly deferred revenue adjustments.
- Operational: burst credits complicate autoscaling and Dedicated capacity planning unless we define strict rules on what counts as "burst" versus baseline.

My recommended path (sales):
1) Offer a conditional managed-burst credit capped at $125k, tied to clear burst gating rules (only applies to spikes above agreed baseline as measured by token/sec and volume windows).
2) Counter the 30% ask with a structured ramp: 20% off year 1 if they commit to the 3-year schedule and meet the minimum committed spend; year 2/3 revert to standard list or graduated discounts.
3) Require the credit to be amortized against committed spend (i.e., applied only after they hit on-the-books ARR thresholds) to protect revenue.

Requesting VP/CFO sign-off to proceed with the counter above. If approved, I'll send the updated term sheet to Sarah (cc Raj) and loop Legal for redline.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@vanguardcare.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@vanguardcare.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal (term sheet v3) — pilot structure + managed-burst option

Sarah / Raj —

Appreciate the conversation earlier — attached is term sheet v3 that captures the pilot structure we discussed. Highlights:
- 3-year commitment with graduated unit pricing (see pricing table, p2).
- Pilot year: 20% introductory discount on per-token inference pricing, subject to minimum committed baseline.
- Managed-burst credit: conditional credit up to $125,000 which applies only to traffic above the agreed weekly baseline and capped monthly.
- Onboarding credit: $50,000 professional services credit to cover model validation and SRE onboarding.

Next steps: please review the term sheet and the usage forecast you shared; Raj, if you can confirm the baseline numbers we talked about I will prepare a clean counter that includes the conditional credit language and the gating rules.

Attachments: vanguardcare-term-sheet-v3.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@vanguardcare.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@vanguardcare.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal (term sheet v3) — pilot structure + managed-burst option

Jonas —

Thanks for the updated doc. Quick notes from our side:
- We really need a stronger onboarding concession to offset integration risk; can you do $150k professional services / credit (instead of $50k)?
- The managed-burst credit is critical for us — we were hoping for $150k to start (unconditional), since our pilot traffic is highly variable and clinical windows may spike unpredictably.
- Also need a 30% unit price discount for year 1 to make the economics work for our clinical teams.

If Redwood can meet those asks, we can commit to the 3-year timeline with the baseline volumes I attached previously.

—Sarah
VP, Platform Engineering, VanguardCare

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: VanguardCare counter-requests — advise on authorization path

Marissa / Grace —

Forwarding Sarah's reply (see below). Their asks: $150k onboarding credit and $150k unconditional managed-burst credit + 30% Y1 discount. My posture: accept $125k managed-burst cap + $50k onboarding credit (we could structure an additional $75k PS credit that vests as usage milestones are achieved). For unit pricing I propose 20% Y1 discount if they sign the 3-year commitment and meet the minimums in year 1.

I went through the numbers with Marcus; the modeled margin impact with a $150k unconditional credit drops below our target threshold for deals in this ARR band unless we amortize and tie to committed spend. 

Proposed language for approval memo to VP/CFO:
- Approve one-off managed-burst credit capped at $125k, to be applied only to spikes above mutually agreed baseline and within monthly caps.
- Approve onboarding PS credit of $50k upfront plus up to $75k contingent that applies only after usage milestones.
- Approve 20% introductory discount in year 1 (not 30%), revert to negotiated levels in later years.
- All credits to be amortized against committed ARR; legal to add revenue recognition schedule.

If we get signoff on the above I will send the revised term sheet and request Legal + Revenue Ops sign the schedule.

Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: VanguardCare counter-requests — advise on authorization path

Jonas / Grace —

After reviewing the proposed counter and the modeled P&L, I approve the conditional concession path with the following non-negotiable controls:
1) Managed-burst credit: capped at $125,000 total and explicitly gated. Define baseline windows and a caps table; credit only applies to traffic above baseline and is applied monthly until the cap is exhausted.
2) Onboarding PS credit: $50,000 upfront; up to $75,000 additional contingent credit that is earned only after the customer hits agreed usage milestones in Q1. No unconditional disbursement of the $75k.
3) Discount: approve a 20% year-1 introductory discount (not 30%). Year 2/3 discounts to be performance-based and revert to standard pricing if minimums are not met.
4) Contracting: Legal to include revenue recognition schedule and a clause preventing downstream reselling of credits. Revenue Ops to confirm amortization schedule.
5) Cap exposure: total credit exposure across all accounts must be tracked; this carveout counts toward our Q2 special-credit budget.

If you implement the redlined language and get Legal/RevOps signs, I am comfortable with this path forward. Please keep precise language in the term sheet so there is no ambiguity on what qualifies as "burst".

Marissa Cole
Chief Financial Officer — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: vanguardcare-redlines.docx
